learning: Five sensing and gain variants have failed the slalom at max_error 0.062 to 0.064, and lead 0.07 m gave no gain (iteration 6). Yaw response is the last untested geometry variable, so this race isolates it.
notes: Runnable package: the Builder's yaw-inertia proposal (mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.12 m) on the iteration 5 sensing, drivetrain and controller. Only the mass and body length differ from the raced design.
rationale: The Builder's proposal changes only the yaw inertia: mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg and body_length 0.16 to 0.12 m. I keep that geometry exactly and take the controller that raced in iteration 5, the best design so far (653.3). Its oval finished 20/20 at 1.85 s, and its s-bend finished 18/20 with steering_oscillation 0.335, under the 0.35 limit. The slalom has failed at max_error 0.062 to 0.064 in every variant tried (span, footprint, lead 0.04, lead 0.07, track), and line loss stayed at about 1.0 events. Lead 0.07 m (iteration 6) gave no gain, so the untested variable is yaw response. Yaw inertia is mass*(body_length^2 + body_width^2)/12, which falls from about 0.00233 to about 0.00144 kg·m^2. A lower inertia should let the robot change heading faster at the slalom's direction changes. The controller needs no change for the new geometry. The sensor span, weights, lead (0.06 m), wheel_track (0.10 m) and wheel_radius (0.03 m) are all unchanged. The off-track limit stays at 0.06 m because body_width is unchanged. kp 3.6 and kd 0.9 are kept so the race isolates the inertia change. The main risk is that faster yaw adds jitter on the s-bend, so steering_oscillation is measured on all three tracks. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events below 1.0 and max_error below 0.06, with the oval still 20/20 and the s-bend at or above 17/20. No outcome is claimed for this package.
